consensus_summary: The seal/mark in the forehead is God's mark of ownership, identification, and protection over His faithful servants (commonly via the Holy Spirit and/or God's name), signifying mind-level allegiance and securing them from judgment, in deliberate contrast to the mark of the beast.
book_summary: The seal is the NAME impressed on its owner—the priestly signet-plate 'HOLINESS TO THE LORD' set by the law on the forehead, the law bound on hand and between the eyes, stamped by the Spirit on God's servants before judgment—with the quoted inscription of 2 Tim 2:19 (the Lord knows His own; depart from iniquity); the counterfeit occupies the same two places.
consensus_core_identification: Divine ownership/identification/protection mark (Spirit and/or name) on the forehead of God's servants.
book_core_identification: The NAME ('HOLINESS TO THE LORD') impressed as priestly signet and law-frontlet, Spirit-stamped, whose content is the 2 Tim 2:19 dual inscription of ownership plus departure from iniquity.
boundary_disagreement: Book tightens the seal's content and conditions around the specific Ex 28 priestly plate, the law as frontlets (hand + forehead), and the dual 2 Tim 2:19 wording (knowledge + moral separation); consensus keeps a broader, less formulaic ownership/Spirit/name category that admits other mechanisms without those exact bounds.
rationale: Both cores identify the forehead seal as God's ownership and identification mark on His people (via name/Spirit), placed before judgment and opposed by a counterfeit on hand/forehead. The book preserves that central referent while materially narrowing its precision and boundary conditions to the concrete NAME-as-signet-plate + law-frontlets + explicit 2 Tim dual inscription; this is refinement of extension and content, not replacement of the referent.
strongest_objection: Consensus primary readings treat Spirit, general ownership, or name as sufficient without elevating the Ex 28 plate or 2 Tim 2:19 dual phrase to definitional status, so the book's typological specificity may appear as added precision rather than the shared core.
